title: Select Sector indices — conditional quarter-end secondary reweighting (24%/4.8%/50% breach test) — the missing Q4 2026 instance
source: EST: rule-derived, not a scheduled publication, and the derivation is this session's own while the rule text is inherited -- that split is stated deliberately rather than blurred. THE RULE, quoted verbatim from the source the sibling entries already carry in this repo (SEC EDGAR, Select Sector SPDR Trust Form 497, accession 0001193125-26-031948, fetched direct 2026-09-05 by the sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-03-31 lane; NOT independently re-fetched by this session, which is the one weakness in this proposal's provenance and is why it is filed as a proposal rather than researched): "if, on the second to last business day of March, June, September, or December a company has a weight greater than 24% or the sum of the companies with weights greater than 4.8% exceeds 50%, a secondary reweighting will be triggered with the reweighting effective date being after the close of the last business day of the month." THE ARITHMETIC IS THIS SESSION'S: December 2026's last business day is Thu 2026-12-31, so the test is struck on the second-to-last business day, Wed 2026-12-30, and the reweighting is effective after the close of Thu 2026-12-31 -- which is the date this id is named for, matching the naming convention the three existing siblings already use (named by the EFFECTIVE date, not the test date). Conditional by construction, so no primary source can pre-confirm that it fires. Discovered during the russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30 initial research, checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30 initial research (2026-09-08), which found it not by reading a new source but by enumerating the calendar while checking whether its own event's Q4 twin was tracked. THIS IS A GAP IN THE MIDDLE OF AN ALREADY-TRACKED SEQUENCE, which is why it is worth filing at all: the calendar carries sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-09-30, -2027-03-31 and -2027-06-30, and carries NO 2026-12-31 entry -- the quarterly test is tracked for three consecutive quarters with the fourth, the year-end one, missing between the first two. The sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-09-30 ledger names it in its own text ("the same conditional test recurs on 2026-12-30, effective after the 2026-12-31 close") and its This-quarter falsifier keys to it, so the gap is a filing omission rather than a deliberate decline. WHY YEAR-END IS THE INSTANCE MOST WORTH HAVING: the Q4 test stacks on the 2026-12-31 corridor the board already tracks -- jpx-market-closure-2026-12-31, sifma-bond-early-close-2026-12-31, china-retaliation-suspension-expiry-2026-12-31, georgia-psc-data-center-cost-shift-2026-12-31 and nerc-computational-load-standards-2026-12-31 -- and it is one session behind the separately proposed russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31, so the two index families' conditional recaps bracket the year-end close. WHAT THE RESEARCHING LANE SHOULD DO FIRST, because this proposal deliberately did not: re-fetch the Form 497 directly rather than inheriting the quote above, and re-run the breach arithmetic under the LIVE capping rule. The 2026-09-30 sibling's research established that the Select Sector capping mechanism was replaced effective 2024-09-23 -- the live rule scales the over-4.8% group down to 45% by relative proportions rather than cutting the smallest member to 4.5% and iterating -- and that the live breach leg this year was XLY's single-company cap on AMZN (24.30% at the 2026-08-14 holdings) rather than any aggregate cohort. Those weights will have been reset by the 2026-12-18 quarterly rebalance before the 12-30 test, so none of the Q3 arithmetic carries over. Impact low and symbols EMPTY to match all three existing siblings. Kind sector matches them too. Filed estimate; the trigger is conditional and no primary can pre-confirm it fires, so this entry can never be promoted to confirmed before the fact.
